2027-01-27.title: Wednesday after Kohne Sunday
readings: Christ and the Church: a great mystery
Marriage is not to be broken
2027-01-27.verse: Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her,
theo: The verse just before today's reading gives a principle for every Christian household: “Be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ.” Mutual self-giving, not domination, is the law of Christian marriage. He then speaks to wives and husbands in the language of his time, but turns everything toward Christ: “Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her.” The measure of a husband's love is the cross. Quoting Genesis, “the two will become one flesh”, Paul adds: “This is a great mystery, and I am applying it to Christ and the church.”

In the Gospel Jesus restores marriage to God's original plan. Moses had allowed a certificate of divorce, but Jesus teaches that the bond is not to be broken. The Church calls marriage a sacrament, a living icon of Christ's faithful love for his Bride; in our tradition the Crowning shows husband and wife as king and queen of a small kingdom, the domestic church. Today let us pray for married couples, for families under strain, and for those whose marriages have been wounded, that they may find in the Church the mercy and truth of Christ.

2027-01-27.prayer: Lord Jesus, you love the Church as a faithful Bridegroom and gave yourself up for her. Bless all married couples with mutual reverence, faithful love and the grace to forgive. Heal wounded families, and make every home a domestic church. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbono is the wedding feast of the Lamb; the self-giving of Christ on the altar is the model of every marriage.

2027-01-27.question: Does my love for my family give itself, as Christ gave himself?

family.explain: St Paul says husbands and wives should love and serve each other the way Jesus loves the Church. Jesus' love is a love that gives everything!
family.intention: We pray for our parents and all married couples.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we serve each other at home today?”

illus: An elderly man in Mavelikara fed his wife, paralysed by a stroke, every meal for eleven years. When the parish priest praised him, he said: on our wedding day I was crowned in church as her king. A king serves his kingdom. She is my kingdom.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, faithful Bridegroom, bless our families and teach us self-giving love. Amen.
share: Be subject to one another (Ephesians 5:21). Where do I insist on my own way?
As Christ loved the church (Ephesians 5:25). Does my love cost me something?
A great mystery (Ephesians 5:32). Do I see marriage as holy?
interc: For married couples, that they may grow in faithful love.
For those whose marriages are wounded.
For young people preparing for marriage.
For our group, that our homes may be domestic churches.
pm.close: Father, you made marriage a sign of Christ's love for the Church. Strengthen our families in that love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, just before today's reading Paul writes: be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ (Ephesians 5:21). Christian marriage is mutual self-giving, not domination.
Then he says: husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her (Ephesians 5:25). The measure of love is the cross.

Quoting Genesis, the two will become one flesh, he adds: this is a great mystery, and I am applying it to Christ and the church (Ephesians 5:32). In the Gospel Jesus teaches that this bond is not to be broken.
In our tradition the Crowning shows husband and wife as king and queen of a domestic church. Let us pray for all couples and for wounded families, that they may find Christ's mercy and truth. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus loves his Church like a good husband loves his wife. Let us pray for our mummy and daddy, and help them at home today!
